environment: A throwaway Postgres started with docker run on an unused port, the backend via mvn spring-boot:run pointed at it, and a production frontend build pointed at that backend — all on OS-assigned ports, driven with playwright-cli. mvn verify and the isolated e2e suite each ran against their own separate throwaway stacks. The developer's docker-compose stack on 5432, 8080 and 3000 was never touched.

steps.note: Fresh non-seeded Agent login: POST /api/me/password with the correct current password returned 204 with a 0-byte body.
The new password signs in (200 with a token); the old one is refused 401.
Repeated for a fresh Manager (a raw User row linked to neither an Agent nor a Tester), an Agent and a Tester; all three succeeded.
Wrong current password returns 400 with code WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD, and the unchanged password still signs in afterwards.
No Authorization header returns 401. All three seeded role tokens given a wrong current password return 400, never 403 — refused on the field, never on the role.
A 7-character new password returns 400 with code PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT; 8 characters returns 204. Both sides of the boundary.

Creating an Agent and a Tester each with a 7-character password are both refused 400 in the ordinary Bean Validation shape. AuthLoginTest's diff against main is empty and the class was run for real: 4 tests, 0 failures — the evidence nobody is locked out.
Exactly one PASSWORD_CHANGED audit line naming entityId, actorUserId and tenantId. The whole log was grepped for the old password, the new password and a bcrypt prefix — none present.
The diff against main contains no migration, an empty SecurityConfig diff, an empty lib/nav.tsx diff, and neither login service at all.

mvn verify 529 tests 0 failures; vitest 186/186; tsc exit 0; eslint clean; isolated e2e read from Playwright's own summary line as 59 passed 0 failed; the visual suite run deliberately (it is not part of verify) as 40 passed, with no golden updated.
The viewer chip opens the identical menu — exactly Change password and Log out — in the Manager, Agent and Client consoles.
Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the chip; reopening and clicking outside does the same.
Keyboard only: Tab to the chip, Enter opens with focus on the first item, arrows cycle both items, Enter activates and focus lands in the dialog's Current password field.

A mismatched confirmation is caught in the browser with no network request fired, proved from the request log. A wrong current password shows an inline alert naming the field, marks it invalid, and keeps every typed value.
A real change redirects to /login?passwordChanged=1 with a status region reading the confirmation.
Signed in with the new password, logged out through the menu, and the old password is then refused with the sign-in page's existing wording — no new message was introduced.
At 390x844 the chip is present and clickable and the menu panel's bounding box sits fully inside the viewport; the same change completes with the same confirmation.
Tabbing chip to menu items to the three dialog fields to Cancel to submit showed a solid 2px focus-visible outline at every stop, confirmed by computed style and a screenshot.
Wording and behaviour parity across the three consoles' menus.
Sign-off that moving Log out into the chip menu is accepted.
Sign-off that neither the menu item nor the dialog title uses the word account, and that it is discoverable.
Your own live password change, plus the second-browser check that the other session survives until it expires.
Review of the DESIGN.md diff alongside the code commit.
